headline: From Russian cages to Irish sanctuary: Two bears find healing
meta_description: After five years and involvement from over 100 people across three countries, two brown bears rescued from cruel confinement in Russia have arrived at an Irish…
summary_short: Two brown bears, one from a circus and one confined to a 2.5m cage, have completed a five-year rescue journey to Wild Ireland sanctuary in County Donegal, overcoming war…
body:
After five years navigating international borders, two wars, and the dedication of more than 100 people, two brown bears have found sanctuary in the Irish countryside. Bu spent years performing in a circus before confinement; Tyapa lived in a cage measuring just 2.5 metres by 2.5 metres by 2 metres—too low for him to stand upright, with no roof to shield him from harsh winters and summer heat. Both arrived severely malnourished with signs of psychological trauma and serious kidney problems from prolonged dehydration. Today, at Wild Ireland in County Donegal, they are adjusting to a totally different world, their coats improving and kidney function returning to normal.

The rescue operation, coordinated by sanctuary founder Killian McLaughlin beginning in 2021, faced extraordinary obstacles. When Russia's invasion of Ukraine made the original transport route impossible in February 2022, organisers pivoted to a Middle Eastern route. But that plan too was disrupted in February 2026 when escalating conflict closed airspace across the region. In late October 2025, a team drove 36 hours to Dagestan to cut the bears from their rusting steel cages, sedate them, and transport them to Tiger House near St Petersburg for veterinary care. After months of preparation, the bears travelled from Moscow via Abu Dhabi, finally arriving in Dublin in August.

At Wild Ireland, the transformation continues. Staff hide food around the woodland habitat to encourage natural foraging behaviour, and both bears' confidence visibly builds week by week. As team member Chloe McElhatton observes, watching them explore grass and soil for the first time represents genuine recovery from trauma. Visitors and locals alike have been moved by their arrival, seeing in these bears not just impressive animals, but survivors whose suffering has ended and whose future now holds the possibility of peace.
quick_facts: Two brown bears rescued from Russia to Wild Ireland in County Donegal, Ireland
Tyapa's cage measured 2.5m × 2.5m × 2m with no roof
Five-year rescue mission delayed by Ukraine invasion and Iran conflict
Over 100 people involved across Russia, UAE, and Ireland
Bears' kidney function and coat health improved significantly since arrival
